title: Fever / Undifferentiated Infection Differential Diagnosis
description: Differential diagnosis for fever and undifferentiated infection in adults, covering infectious, neoplastic, rheumatic/inflammatory, and miscellaneous etiologies. Organized by the classic four-category framework for systematic fever workup.
source_description: Cunha BA. Fever of unknown origin: clinical overview of classic and current concepts. Infect Dis Clin North Am. 2007 Dec;21(4):867-915.

diagnoses.name: Sepsis / Septic Shock
key_features: Hypotension refractory to fluid resuscitation (septic shock)
Known or suspected source of infection
red_flags: Mean arterial pressure <65 mmHg despite fluids

diagnoses.name: Bacterial Pneumonia
key_features: Focal crackles or bronchial breath sounds on auscultation

diagnoses.name: Urinary Tract Infection / Pyelonephritis
key_features: Flank pain and costovertebral angle tenderness (pyelonephritis)
red_flags: Obstructing ureteral stone with infected hydronephrosis
recommended_tests: CT abdomen/pelvis if complicated or no response to therapy

diagnoses.name: Bacterial Meningitis
key_features: Classic triad: fever, neck stiffness, altered consciousness
recommended_tests: CT head before LP if focal neurological signs

diagnoses.name: Infective Endocarditis
key_features: Persistent fever with new or changing heart murmur
Peripheral embolic phenomena (Janeway lesions, Osler nodes, splinter hemorrhages)
Positive blood cultures (often Staphylococcus or Streptococcus)
Predisposing valve disease or IV drug use
red_flags: Acute valvular regurgitation with heart failure
recommended_tests: Blood cultures (3 sets from separate sites)

diagnoses.name: Intra-abdominal Abscess
key_features: Fever with localized abdominal pain or tenderness
History of recent surgery, diverticulitis, or appendicitis
Palpable mass or localized peritoneal signs
Failure of fever to resolve with appropriate antibiotics

diagnoses.name: Lymphoma
key_features: Prolonged fever with night sweats and weight loss (B symptoms)
Pel-Ebstein fever pattern (periodic fevers in Hodgkin lymphoma)
recommended_tests: CBC with differential and peripheral smear

diagnoses.name: Drug Fever
key_features: Fever temporally related to drug initiation (usually 7-10 days)
Patient appears well despite high fever
red_flags: Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis

diagnoses.name: Adult-Onset Still Disease
key_features: Quotidian (daily) high spiking fevers with return to baseline
red_flags: Macrophage activation syndrome (cytopenias, coagulopathy, liver failure)
recommended_tests: Glycosylated ferritin fraction (<20% suggests Still disease)

diagnoses.name: Tuberculosis (Pulmonary and Extrapulmonary)
key_features: Prolonged low-grade fever with night sweats
History of TB exposure, endemic area, or immunosuppression
red_flags: Miliary pattern on chest X-ray (disseminated TB)
TB meningitis (altered mental status, cranial nerve palsies)
recommended_tests: Sputum AFB smear and culture (3 specimens)
Interferon-gamma release assay or tuberculin skin test

diagnoses.name: Viral Syndrome (Self-Limited)
key_features: Acute onset fever with myalgias and malaise
Upper respiratory symptoms (rhinorrhea, sore throat, cough)
recommended_tests: Influenza and COVID-19 testing during epidemic seasons

diagnoses.name: Skin and Soft Tissue Infection (Cellulitis/Abscess)
key_features: Localized erythema, warmth, swelling, and tenderness
red_flags: Pain out of proportion to exam findings
recommended_tests: CT or MRI if necrotizing fasciitis suspected

also_consider.name: Malaria
also_consider.rationale: Must be considered in any febrile patient with travel to endemic area; thick and thin blood smears or rapid diagnostic test are diagnostic

also_consider.name: HIV Acute Retroviral Syndrome
also_consider.rationale: Fever, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, and rash 2-4 weeks after exposure; standard HIV antibody may be negative early, order HIV RNA viral load

also_consider.name: Subacute Thyroiditis (de Quervain)
also_consider.rationale: Fever with anterior neck pain and tender thyroid; elevated ESR with transient thyrotoxicosis followed by hypothyroidism

also_consider.name: Giant Cell (Temporal) Arteritis
also_consider.rationale: New headache, jaw claudication, and elevated ESR in adults over 50; risk of irreversible vision loss requires urgent corticosteroids

also_consider.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
also_consider.rationale: Fever in young women with multisystem involvement (arthritis, serositis, rash, cytopenias); check ANA and anti-dsDNA

also_consider.name: Pulmonary Embolism
also_consider.rationale: Low-grade fever occurs in up to 14% of PE cases; consider in febrile patients with pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, and risk factors for VTE

also_consider.name: Factitious Fever
also_consider.rationale: Discrepancy between high recorded temperature and clinical appearance; observed temperature measurement is diagnostic

also_consider.name: Hepatic Abscess (Pyogenic or Amoebic)
also_consider.rationale: Fever with right upper quadrant pain and elevated alkaline phosphatase; travel history raises suspicion for amoebic etiology

also_consider.name: Osteomyelitis
also_consider.rationale: Persistent fever with focal bone pain; often hematogenous in elderly or contiguous with diabetic foot infections; MRI is imaging of choice

also_consider.name: Sarcoidosis
also_consider.rationale: Fever with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, erythema nodosum, and elevated ACE level; noncaseating granulomas on biopsy

also_consider.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Crohn Disease)
also_consider.rationale: Fever with chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss; extraintestinal manifestations may precede GI symptoms

also_consider.name: Alcoholic Hepatitis
also_consider.rationale: Fever with jaundice, hepatomegaly, and elevated AST:ALT ratio >2 in a patient with heavy alcohol use

also_consider.name: Catheter-Related Bloodstream Infection
also_consider.rationale: Fever in a patient with an indwelling vascular catheter; differential time to positivity of blood cultures aids diagnosis

also_consider.name: Prosthetic Joint or Device Infection
also_consider.rationale: Low-grade fever with pain at prosthetic site; may present months to years after implantation; joint aspiration is key diagnostic step

also_consider.name: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
also_consider.rationale: High fever, muscle rigidity, altered mental status, and autonomic instability after dopamine antagonist initiation or dose change; CK markedly elevated

clinical_reasoning_prompt: This is an evidence-based reference set, not an exhaustive differential. The four classic categories of fever etiology are infectious (most common), neoplastic, rheumatic/inflammatory, and miscellaneous. Consider the patient's immune status, medication history, travel and exposure history, duration of fever, and fever pattern when narrowing the differential. In patients with undifferentiated fever, always assess for sepsis urgently before pursuing a systematic diagnostic workup. Atypical presentations are common in the elderly, immunosuppressed, and those on antipyretics or corticosteroids.
